reason: This comment asks a question about our data rather than requesting a change, and the answer does not imply one. We cross-referenced the FACT-Seq HIV-specific clonotypes against the unstimulated repertoire and report the result in full in the response: 3 of 72 recover at the clonotype level for CP018, and 31 of 72 when any stimulated clonotype is considered. No claim in the manuscript asserts a higher level of confirmation, so there is no statement to correct. We note one point that may merit a Methods sentence if the editor prefers: matching on the strict clonotype definition initially returned zero matches because Cell Ranger 9.0.1 and 10.1.0 write the empty D-gene field differently, an artefact rather than a biological absence. This concerns our cross-referencing procedure rather than any published result.
Cohort-wide realignment completed for the nine entry-visit libraries; detection, the three controls and per-cell burden are reported in the response and in HIV_cohort_*.csv.

Antibody clones, catalogue numbers and barcode sequences, the FACT-Seq sort instrument, and the sequencing chemistry version are laboratory records. The ADT panel composition and the Cell Ranger version and reference build have been recovered from the data and are given, but the remaining details exist only in lab documentation.

Editorial decision. Additional data are now provided: the same FACT-Seq protocol was run in a second participant (CP018) in technical duplicate at both timepoints, so the antigen-specificity method reproduces independently. Whether that meets the replication policy, or an exception is needed, is for the editor; the request goes in the cover letter.
